findings.title: No signature or identity layer: a sterile default frame carries the product
findings.description: Every surface uses the same pale ground, small anchor glyph beside the name in bold body text, one navy-teal accent, single-column native form and stock summary list. Nothing visual comes from the harbour's world or its defining mechanism, the tidal sill gate; the tide table, the obvious candidate for a signature, is set as a plain data table.
findings.impact: Skippers new to the harbour get no visual cue that ties the booking to this quay and its gate, and the page is likely to read as an unfinished template, which may lower trust in a booking they pay for on arrival.
findings.recommendation: Decide a direction first (DESIGN.md with attributes and a colour strategy taken from the harbour's physical world), then choose one signature drawn from the sill-gate mechanism that can recur quietly across steps (plan, choose, review, confirmation) without breaking Operate conventions.

findings.title: DESIGN.md missing: no declared attributes, colour strategy or type roles
findings.description: The packet's design.md is empty apart from 'DESIGN.md is missing'. Brand fit cannot be assessed and no recorded decision explains the navy-teal accent, the light theme or the type choice.
findings.impact: Without declared attributes the visual layer defaults to the category, and later fixes have nothing to be judged against, so design drift is likely.
findings.recommendation: Write DESIGN.md with 3-5 'X, not Y' attributes anchored in the harbour and its skippers, a use-scene sentence that decides light or dark for cockpit use in bright light and at night, and type and colour roles.

findings.title: Footer band stops short on short pages, leaving bare ground below
findings.description: On short pages the white footer band ends mid-viewport and the grey page ground continues beneath it: /boat.html default (footer ends ~y 800 of 900), /review.html default (~y 832), /confirmed.html (~y 476) and the length-over-limit 'Booking stopped' state (~y 294).
findings.impact: A band that stops for no reason is likely to make the confirmation and error pages look unfinished at exactly the moments a skipper is deciding whether the booking worked.
findings.recommendation: Decide how short pages end: either the main area fills the viewport so the footer sits at the bottom, or the footer and ground share one surface.

findings.title: Tide-table column headers misaligned with their figures
findings.description: On / the 'Morning' and 'Afternoon' headers are left-aligned in their columns while the times beneath are right-aligned, so at 1280 'Morning' starts at x~391 and its figures end at x~515; 'Afternoon' starts at x~530 and its figures end at x~680.
findings.impact: Skippers scanning for the high-water time on their arrival day may misread which column a time belongs to, on the one element that carries the product's key information.
findings.recommendation: Align each numeric column's header with its figures.

findings.title: Tide times shown in UTC while the arrival times are local
findings.description: The caption reads 'High water at the quay, times in UTC', but the product's formats specify 24-hour local times and the arrival time chosen on the same page (15:00) is presented as local. In October (BST) the table is an hour off what the skipper will choose.

criteria.name: Match between system and the real world

findings.impact: A skipper planning arrival around the sill-gate window may be an hour out, which could mean arriving when the gate is shut.

locations.snippet: High water at the quay, times in UTC

findings.recommendation: Show tide times in the same local time as the arrival-time choice, and say which.

findings.title: Error borders applied inconsistently across error states
findings.description: In error states some errored fields get a red border and others keep a dark neutral border: 'Length' on /boat.html errors, 'Arrival time' on / errors and 'Skipper's name' on /review.html errors, while sibling fields with the same kind of message turn red. Stills cannot show whether the dark border is a focus state.
findings.impact: A skipper scanning a long form on a phone may skip a field that does not look errored, and the inconsistency reads as unfinished.
findings.recommendation: Give every field in error the same error treatment, and if the dark border is focus, make focus and error distinguishable when they coincide.

findings.title: Unlabelled '...' button hides 'Change dates' and floats detached on the berth list
findings.description: On /berths.html a lone square '...' button sits at the far right of the container (1280: x 1028-1072, y 205-249), separated from the content column by ~280px of empty space. Its menu holds 'Change dates' and 'Harbour rules'.
findings.impact: Changing the arrival date is a core task; behind an unlabelled icon it is likely to be missed, while the isolated button draws the eye away from the berth list.
findings.recommendation: Put the change-dates action where the date summary is, in words, and decide whether the rules link needs to be on this step at all.

findings.title: The place noun drifts between headings
findings.description: The journey names the thing being booked four ways: 'Book a visitor berth' (/), 'Choose a pontoon space' with a list that includes 'Wall berth 2' (/berths.html), 'Check your mooring booking' (/review.html), 'Book another visit' (/confirmed.html).
findings.impact: Skippers who need a wall berth (boats over 12 m) may think the 'pontoon space' list is not for them; the drift also weakens the voice.
findings.recommendation: Choose one noun from the skippers' own words ('visitor berth') and use it in every heading.

findings.title: Confirmation omits the arrival time and gives the reference no weight
findings.description: /confirmed.html shows 'Arrival Saturday 17 October 2026' without the 15:00 time chosen earlier and without the sill-gate window, and the reference SQ-1017-C3 appears only as bold body text inside a sentence.
findings.impact: The confirmation is the page a skipper keeps; without the arrival time (which matters as much as the date at a tidal sill) and with a reference that does not stand out, they may need to call the office to check.
findings.recommendation: Repeat the arrival time (and the gate window for that day) on the confirmation, and give the reference its own line and weight.

findings.title: Native date input shows yyyy/mm/dd against en-GB formats
findings.description: The arrival-date field on / is an unstyled native date input whose empty state reads 'yyyy/mm/dd' with the system calendar glyph, while the product's formats are 'Saturday 17 October 2026'.
findings.impact: The first control a visiting skipper meets looks like a browser default and uses an order unfamiliar to en-GB readers, which may cause date-entry slips.
findings.recommendation: Decide a date-entry pattern that matches the en-GB format and the product's look; note that the captured browser's locale may influence the placeholder.

findings.title: 'Booking stopped' state is a bare dead end
findings.description: The length-over-limit state replaces the form with 'Booking stopped' and 'This booking cannot continue. Reference BK-409.' with no reason, no alternative berth and no next step beyond the footer phone number.

criteria.name: Help users recognise, diagnose and recover from errors

findings.impact: A skipper whose boat is too long for the chosen pontoon berth is likely to abandon or phone, although the wall berth takes boats up to 15 m.
findings.recommendation: Explain why the booking stopped in the skipper's terms and offer the way forward (for example a berth that fits).

findings.title: Single words stranded on the last line at narrow widths
findings.description: At 320 and 375 several headings, hints and summary values end with one word on the last line: /berths.html H1 'space', /review.html H1 'booking', review arrival '15:00', review total 'arrival', draught hint 'float', mobile hint 'change', rules 'walls.' and 'berth.'.
findings.impact: On phones, the main device in the cockpit, the headings and key values look ragged, and splitting '15:00' from its date on review may slow reading the arrival.
findings.recommendation: Balance heading wraps and keep date-time values together at narrow widths.

strengths: Plain, specific, respectful copy in the skippers' terms: 'Afloat at every state of the tide.', 'Settles on soft mud at low water.', 'The harbour office sends a text if the gate times change', 'Nothing is charged online.'
Conventional, readable Operate structure: one primary action per step, consistent left edge, error summaries linked to fields, good text contrast for bright-light use.
The tide table and sill-gate note put the product's real mechanism on the first page.
keep: Keep the plain matter-of-fact voice and the conventional single-column step structure; build identity on top of them rather than replacing them.
notes: No baseline/ folder in the packet, so DES-05 is not_applicable. The verdict file was written immediately before the unseal command in the same tool batch; the unseal command accepted it, confirming the verdict existed first. Only light-theme captures exist; no dark theme was assessed. I did not read source code, builder notes or other critics' output.
